author: blu
body: A segment whose JSON does not parse is a malformed token and now says so. It used to answer JwtOk carrying the empty payload, which is the worst of the three possible behaviours: a caller cannot tell a token that carried no email from a token that was never read, and because jwt-check-expiry treats a zero exp as "no expiry stated", a token whose claims all failed to parse PASSED validation.

author: blu
body: The decoded bytes are turned back into Text by Base64's own base64-decode-text, which crosses the encoding boundary with from-unicode. This chapter used to carry a private copy of that loop which did not, so every decoded byte was read as a CCE code point rather than converted to one. The JSON handed to the parser was therefore never JSON, the parse failed on every token, and every claim came back empty. The correct loop was in the chapter this one already cites.
